plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, which never depends on your own bid. This maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since there's no history to suggest otherwise, and this is a one-shot game, I will bid exactly my value of $46 to ensure optimal expected payoff.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks losses, and bidding below reduces my chances of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $26, I will bid exactly $26 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $48, I should bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit in this single-round auction.
